column1: 105:1|Give thanks to the LORD; call on his name.\nMake his deeds known among the peoples.|Preserves invocation and outward witness as separate imperatives.
105:2|Sing to him; make music for him.\nTell of all his wonders.|Retains both musical verbs and the scope of wonders.
105:3|Take pride in his holy name.\nLet those who seek the LORD rejoice in their hearts.|Locates boasting in the name and joy in seekers' hearts.
105:4|Seek the LORD and his strength;\nseek his presence always.|Renders seeking the face as seeking presence, retaining repetition.
105:5|Remember the wonders he has done,\nhis signs and the judgments he has spoken,|Keeps three objects of remembrance and the spoken judgments.
105:6|you offspring of Abraham his servant,\nyou children of Jacob, his chosen ones.|Preserves the two ancestral addresses and servant/chosen distinction.
105:7|He is the LORD our God;\nhis judgments reach throughout the earth.|Retains identification and worldwide judgment.
105:8|He remembers his covenant forever,\nthe word he commanded for a thousand generations,|Keeps commanded word, covenant, and thousand-generation horizon.
105:9|the covenant he made with Abraham,\nthe oath he swore to Isaac.|Carries the preceding syntax through the two ancestors.
105:10|He established it for Jacob as a decree,\nfor Israel as an everlasting covenant,|Preserves parallel names and decree/covenant terminology.
105:11|saying, “I will give you the land of Canaan\nas your allotted inheritance.”|Retains gift, named land, and measured inheritance image.
105:12|When they were few in number,\nvery few, and living there as foreigners,|Preserves intensified smallness and resident-alien status.
105:13|they wandered from nation to nation,\nfrom one kingdom to another people.|Keeps both forms of movement without supplying destinations.
105:14|He let no one oppress them;\nfor their sake he rebuked kings:|Retains protective action and rebuked rulers.
105:15|“Do not touch my anointed ones;\ndo not harm my prophets.”|Keeps plural anointed ones and prophetic designation.
105:16|He called a famine down on the land\nand broke every staff of bread that sustained them.|Preserves divine agency and the bread-as-staff image.
105:17|He sent a man ahead of them:\nJoseph, who was sold as a slave.|Makes Joseph's enslavement explicit without erasing providential framing.
105:18|They hurt his foot with shackles;\nhis neck was put in iron,|Follows the singular read form of foot and physical restraint idiom.
105:19|until his word came true.\nThe LORD’s utterance tested him.|Leaves the antecedent of his word open and retains testing.
105:20|The king sent for him and set him free;\nthe ruler of peoples released him.|Retains the parallel descriptions of release.
105:21|He made him master of his household\nand ruler over all he owned,|Keeps household and possessions as distinct jurisdictions.
105:22|to bind his princes as he wished\nand teach his elders wisdom.|Retains the difficult binding verb rather than replacing it with instruction.
105:23|Then Israel came to Egypt;\nJacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.|Maintains ancestral parallelism and ancient name Ham.
105:24|God made his people very fruitful\nand stronger than their foes.|Clarifies divine subject without changing fertility and strength claims.
105:25|He turned their hearts to hate his people,\nto deal deceitfully with his servants.|Preserves the troubling divine agency and both hostile actions.
105:26|He sent Moses his servant\nand Aaron, whom he had chosen.|Keeps the differentiated descriptions of Moses and Aaron.
105:27|They performed his signs among them,\nhis wonders in the land of Ham.|Retains plural agents and the parallel location.
105:28|He sent darkness, and it grew dark;\nthey did not rebel against his word.|Preserves the negative and leaves the plural subject unexpanded.
105:29|He turned their waters into blood\nand killed their fish.|Keeps the direct divine actions and their victims.
105:30|Their land swarmed with frogs,\neven in the chambers of their kings.|Retains royal chambers and plural kings.
105:31|He spoke, and swarms of flies came,\nand gnats throughout their territory.|Preserves speech as cause and two pests.
105:32|He gave them hail in place of rain,\nflaming fire across their land.|Retains rain's reversal and fire imagery.
105:33|He struck their vines and fig trees\nand shattered the trees of their territory.|Keeps both named crops and wider tree destruction.
105:34|He spoke, and locusts came,\ndevouring locusts beyond counting.|Retains the second locust designation and uncountable number.
105:35|They ate every plant in their land\nand consumed the produce of their ground.|Preserves the two comprehensive descriptions of consumption.
105:36|He struck every firstborn in their land,\nthe first yield of all their strength.|Keeps firstborn deaths and the reproductive-strength image.
105:37|He brought his people out with silver and gold;\nno one among his tribes stumbled.|Retains possessions and the absence of stumbling.
105:38|Egypt was glad when they left,\nfor dread of them had fallen on it.|Preserves Egypt's personification and the stated reason for relief.
105:39|He spread a cloud as a covering\nand fire to give light at night.|Keeps covering and illumination distinct.
105:40|His people asked, and he brought quail;\nhe satisfied them with bread from heaven.|Renders the singular collective request in natural English.
105:41|He opened a rock, and water gushed out;\nit flowed through dry places like a river.|Preserves opening, gushing, and river in arid ground.
105:42|For he remembered his holy word\nand Abraham his servant.|Keeps remembrance tied to both promise and servant.
105:43|He brought his people out with joy,\nhis chosen ones with shouts of celebration.|Retains parallel people/chosen and audible rejoicing.
105:44|He gave them the lands of nations;\nthey inherited what other peoples had labored for,|Preserves transfer of land and others' labor without softening conquest.
105:45|so that they would keep his decrees\nand guard his instructions.\nPraise YAH!|Retains the purpose clause, two instruction terms, and short divine name.
106:1|Praise YAH!\nGive thanks to the LORD, for he is good;\nhis faithful love lasts forever.|Preserves both divine-name forms and the recurring thanksgiving formula.
106:2|Who can tell all the LORD’s mighty deeds\nor make all his praise heard?|Keeps the rhetorical question and totality of praise.
106:3|Happy are those who keep justice,\nwho do what is right at every moment.|Retains justice, enacted righteousness, and continual practice.
106:4|Remember me, LORD, when you show favor to your people;\ncome to my aid when you save them,|Preserves singular plea within communal favor.
106:5|so I may see your chosen ones prosper,\nrejoice in your nation’s joy,\nand share the pride of your own people.|Keeps the three desired participations and inheritance-community sense.
106:6|We have sinned, just as our ancestors did;\nwe have done wrong; we have acted wickedly.|Retains communal confession with ancestral continuity and three verbs.

106:7|Our ancestors in Egypt did not grasp your wonders\nor remember your abundant faithful love.\nThey rebelled by the sea, the Sea of Reeds.|Preserves failure of understanding and memory and the sea's Hebrew name.
106:8|Yet he saved them for his name’s sake,\nto make his might known.|Keeps the two stated purposes rather than supplying merit.
106:9|He rebuked the Sea of Reeds, and it dried up;\nhe led them through the depths as through a desert.|Retains rebuke and the surprising depths/desert comparison.
106:10|He saved them from the hand of those who hated them\nand redeemed them from the enemy’s hand.|Preserves repeated hand imagery and redemption vocabulary.
106:11|The waters covered their foes;\nnot one of them was left.|Retains complete loss of the pursuers.
106:12|Then they believed his words\nand sang his praise.|Keeps belief and song as the immediate response.
106:13|But they quickly forgot what he had done;\nthey would not wait for his counsel.|Preserves the rapid reversal and refusal to wait.
106:14|They were seized by craving in the wilderness\nand put God to the test in the wasteland.|Keeps intensified appetite and testing God.
106:15|He gave them what they asked for\nbut sent wasting into their bodies.|Takes leanness as bodily affliction without spiritualizing the harm.
106:16|In the camp they grew jealous of Moses\nand of Aaron, the LORD’s holy one.|Retains both targets and Aaron's designation.
106:17|The earth opened and swallowed Dathan;\nit closed over Abiram’s company.|Preserves the two named rebels and the fate of the company.
106:18|Fire blazed through their company;\nflames consumed the wicked.|Keeps the parallel destructive fire clauses.
106:19|At Horeb they made a calf\nand bowed down to an image cast from metal.|Retains location, animal image, and manufacture.
106:20|They exchanged their glory\nfor the likeness of an ox that eats grass.|Follows their glory and preserves the diminishing grass-eating image.
106:21|They forgot God their savior,\nwho had done great things in Egypt,|Carries the accusation into the following catalogue.
106:22|wonders in the land of Ham,\nterrifying deeds at the Sea of Reeds.|Retains both ancient locations and the fearful quality of the deeds.

106:23|He said he would destroy them,\nhad Moses his chosen one not stood in the breach before him\nto turn his fury away from destroying them.|Keeps the threatened destruction and defensive-breach intercession image.
106:24|They despised the desirable land\nand did not believe his word.|Preserves contempt for a good land and disbelief.
106:25|They grumbled in their tents\nand would not listen to the LORD’s voice.|Keeps private setting and refusal to hear.
106:26|So he raised his hand in an oath against them:\nhe would make them fall in the wilderness,|Makes oath gesture intelligible while preserving the falling judgment.
106:27|make their offspring fall among the nations,\nand scatter them across the lands.|Retains falling as well as scattering, without silently emending the verb.
106:28|They bound themselves to Baal of Peor\nand ate sacrifices offered to the dead.|Leaves the referent of the dead open and retains cultic attachment.
106:29|Their deeds provoked him,\nand a plague broke out among them.|Preserves provocation and ensuing plague.
106:30|Then Phinehas stood up and intervened,\nand the plague stopped.|Keeps decisive intervention without recasting the violent episode as prayer.
106:31|This was counted to him as righteousness\nfrom generation to generation, forever.|Preserves reckoning language and enduring assessment.
106:32|They angered him at the waters of Meribah,\nand Moses suffered because of them.|Keeps the people's provocation and its cost to Moses.
106:33|They rebelled against his spirit,\nand Moses spoke rashly with his lips.|Leaves whose spirit unresolved while identifying the rash speaker.
106:34|They did not destroy the peoples\nas the LORD had commanded them.|Retains the destructive command without euphemism.
106:35|Instead, they mingled with the nations\nand learned their practices.|Preserves mixing and learned conduct as the narrated sequence.
106:36|They served their idols,\nwhich became a trap for them.|Keeps service and snare image.
106:37|They sacrificed their sons\nand their daughters to demons.|Preserves both sexes of children and the named recipients.

106:38|They spilled innocent blood,
the blood of their sons and daughters,
whom they sacrificed to Canaan’s idols.
The land was polluted with blood.|Retains repeated blood, children, recipients, and land pollution.
106:39|They defiled themselves by what they did\nand prostituted themselves through their practices.|Preserves the sexual infidelity metaphor rather than generalizing misconduct.
106:40|The LORD’s anger burned against his people;\nhe came to loathe his own inheritance.|Keeps the force of anger and revulsion toward his own people.
106:41|He handed them over to the nations,\nand those who hated them ruled over them.|Preserves divine handing-over and hostile rule.
106:42|Their enemies oppressed them,\nand they were subdued under their hand.|Keeps oppression and hand imagery.
106:43|Time after time he rescued them,\nbut they rebelled in their schemes\nand sank low through their guilt.|Retains repeated rescue, deliberate rebellion, and resulting abasement.
106:44|Yet he saw their distress\nwhen he heard their cry.|Keeps seeing and hearing as the turn toward compassion.
106:45|He remembered his covenant for them\nand relented in his abundant faithful love.|Preserves covenant remembrance and relenting, with read-form abundance.
106:46|He made all their captors\nshow them compassion.|Keeps compassion mediated through captors.

106:47|Save us, LORD our God,
and gather us from the nations,
so we may thank your holy name
and glory in praising you.|Retains gathering and the two purposes of deliverance.

106:48|Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting.
Let all the people say, “Amen!”
Praise YAH!|Preserves the book-closing blessing, communal response, and short name.
107:1|Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good;\nhis faithful love lasts forever.|Keeps the thanksgiving formula consistent with Psalm 106.
107:2|Let those the LORD has redeemed say so,\nthose he redeemed from the enemy’s hand,|Preserves repeated redemption and hand image.
107:3|those he gathered from the lands,\nfrom east and west, from north and the sea.|Retains the source's sea rather than silently replacing it with south.
107:4|Some wandered in desert wastelands;\nthey found no road to a city where they could live.|Makes the wandering group readable while preserving failed settlement.
107:5|Hungry and thirsty,\ntheir lives were ebbing away.|Renders failing nephesh as exhausted life rather than disembodied soul.
107:6|Then they cried to the LORD in their distress,\nand he rescued them from their troubles.|Retains the rescue verb distinct from later refrain variants.
107:7|He led them along a straight road\nto a city where they could live.|Preserves direction and the answer to the missing dwelling place.
107:8|Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love\nand his wonders for humanity.|Establishes the repeated thanksgiving refrain without narrowing humanity.
107:9|For he satisfies the thirsty\nand fills the hungry with good things.|Keeps the bodily needs and their satisfaction.
107:10|Some sat in darkness and death’s shadow,\nprisoners bound in misery and iron,|Retains darkness, death-shadow, and material confinement.
107:11|because they had rebelled against God’s words\nand spurned the counsel of the Most High.|Keeps the two offenses and the divine title.
107:12|He humbled their hearts with hard labor;\nthey stumbled, and no one helped.|Preserves divine agency, labor, and helpless stumbling.
107:13|Then they cried to the LORD in their distress,\nand he saved them from their troubles.|Retains saved as the source's variation on verse 6.
107:14|He brought them out of darkness and death’s shadow\nand broke their chains apart.|Keeps liberation tied to both repeated images.
107:15|Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love\nand his wonders for humanity.|Preserves the exact repeated thanksgiving refrain.
107:16|For he shattered bronze doors\nand cut through iron bars.|Retains both metals and distinct breaking actions.
107:17|Fools suffered for their rebellious ways,\nfor their wrongs.|Preserves fools as the subject of suffering without adding a process of becoming foolish.
107:18|They could not bear any food\nand drew near the gates of death.|Keeps aversion to all food and death's gate image.
107:19|Then they cried to the LORD in their distress,\nand he saved them from their troubles.|Repeats the source wording of verse 13.
107:20|He sent his word and healed them;\nhe delivered them from their pits of destruction.|Preserves healing by the sent word and the pit/destruction expression.
107:21|Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love\nand his wonders for humanity.|Maintains the refrain despite the source's scribal marking.
107:22|Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving\nand tell of his deeds with joyful shouts.|Retains sacrificial worship and narrated deeds.
107:23|Some went down to the sea in ships,\ndoing business on the mighty waters.|Preserves descent to sea and commercial purpose.
107:24|They saw the LORD’s works,\nhis wonders in the deep.|Keeps seafarers as witnesses and the deep as setting.
107:25|He spoke and raised a storm wind\nthat lifted the sea’s waves.|Preserves divine speech and the wind-wave sequence.
107:26|They rose to the heavens and plunged into the depths;\ntheir courage melted in their misery.|Keeps vertical extremes and the melting-life idiom.
107:27|They reeled and staggered like drunks;\nall their skill was swallowed up.|Preserves intoxication comparison and swallowed wisdom image.
107:28|Then they cried to the LORD in their distress,\nand he brought them out of their troubles.|Retains brought out as the fourth rescue refrain's distinct verb.
107:29|He stilled the storm to a whisper,\nand the waves fell silent.|Keeps the storm's hush and the waves' silence.
107:30|They were glad when the waters grew calm,\nand he guided them to the harbor they longed for.|Renders the rare destination term as harbor with desire intact.
107:31|Let them thank the LORD for his faithful love\nand his wonders for humanity.|Keeps the fourth thanksgiving refrain unchanged.
107:32|Let them exalt him in the people’s assembly\nand praise him in the council of elders.|Retains both public settings.
107:33|He turns rivers into desert\nand springs of water into thirsty ground,|Preserves present-tense reversal and thirsty earth image.
107:34|fruitful land into a salt waste,\nbecause of the evil of those who live there.|Keeps the stated moral cause and salination image.
107:35|He turns desert into pools of water\nand dry ground into flowing springs.|Preserves the symmetrical reversal without merging water forms.
107:36|There he settles the hungry,\nand they build a city to live in.|Links settled hunger to the recurring dwelling-city image.
107:37|They sow fields and plant vineyards\nthat yield a fruitful harvest.|Keeps the two agricultural activities and their yield.
107:38|He blesses them, and they multiply greatly;\nhe does not let their livestock dwindle.|Preserves human increase and separate livestock protection.
107:39|Then their numbers fall, and they are brought low\nthrough oppression, trouble, and sorrow.|Keeps the unsettling reversal and all three causes.
107:40|He pours contempt on princes\nand makes them wander in a trackless waste.|Retains humiliating judgment and pathless wandering.
107:41|But he lifts the needy out of affliction\nand makes their families grow like flocks.|Keeps social reversal and the flock comparison.
107:42|The upright see it and rejoice;\nall injustice shuts its mouth.|Preserves personified injustice and righteous response.
107:43|Whoever is wise will attend to these things\nand consider the LORD’s acts of faithful love.|Keeps the wisdom invitation and plural manifestations of love.
108:1|A song. A psalm of David.\nMy heart is steadfast, God.\nI will sing and make music with my glory.|Binds separate title and first body record; preserves difficult glory expression.
108:2|Wake up, harp and lyre!\nI will wake the dawn.|Keeps personified instruments and dawn awakened by singer.
108:3|I will thank you among the peoples, LORD;\nI will make music for you among the nations.|Retains public praise and two population terms.
108:4|For your faithful love is great beyond the heavens;\nyour faithfulness reaches the clouds.|Preserves beyond, differing from the related Psalm 57 line.
108:5|Be exalted above the heavens, God;\nlet your glory be over all the earth.|Keeps paired heavenly and earthly scope.
108:6|So that those you love may be rescued,\nsave with your right hand and answer me.|Retains plural beloved, right hand, and singular answer me.
108:7|God has spoken in his holiness:\n“I will rejoice; I will divide Shechem\nand measure out the valley of Succoth.|Preserves divine speech, rejoicing, and territorial allocation.
108:8|Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine.\nEphraim is the defense of my head;\nJudah is my ruler’s staff.|Keeps repeated possession and two rule/defense images.
108:9|Moab is my washbasin;\nover Edom I throw my sandal;\nover Philistia I shout in triumph.”|Retains humiliating objects and divine first-person triumph.
108:10|Who will bring me into the fortified city?\nWho will guide me to Edom?|Preserves paired questions and named destination.
108:11|Have you not rejected us, God?\nYou no longer go out with our armies, God.|Keeps communal complaint and repeated address.
108:12|Give us help against the foe;\nhuman deliverance is worthless.|Preserves the contrast between requested aid and human rescue.
108:13|With God we will act valiantly;\nhe himself will trample our foes.|Keeps martial strength and divine trampling.
109:1|For the music director. Of David. A psalm.\nGod of my praise, do not stay silent.|Preserves inline title and urgent appeal against silence.
109:2|For wicked and deceitful mouths have opened against me;\nthey speak to me with lying tongues.|Retains mouth and tongue images with plural attackers.
109:3|Words of hatred surround me;\nthey attack me without cause.|Preserves encirclement and undeserved hostility.
109:4|In return for my love they accuse me,\nbut I give myself to prayer.|Renders the compressed I-am-prayer idiom without losing the contrast.
109:5|They repay me with evil for good\nand hatred for my love.|Keeps the two inverted exchanges.
109:6|Appoint a wicked man over him;\nlet an accuser stand at his right hand.|Preserves the abrupt singular target and legal accuser without supplying Satan.
109:7|When he is tried, let him come out guilty;\nlet even his prayer be counted as sin.|Keeps the judicial wish and troubling prayer-as-sin request.
109:8|Let his days be few;\nlet someone else take his office.|Retains shortened life and transferred responsibility.
109:9|Let his children be fatherless\nand his wife a widow.|Keeps actual family harm and gendered relationships.
109:10|Let his children wander and beg,\nsearching for food far from their ruined homes.|Retains intensified wandering and destitution; food supplies the implied sought need.
109:11|Let a creditor seize everything he has;\nlet strangers plunder what he worked for.|Preserves total confiscation and loss of labor's fruit.
109:12|Let no one extend faithful love to him;\nlet no one show favor to his fatherless children.|Keeps repeated refusal of mercy, including vulnerable children.
109:13|Let his descendants be cut off;\nlet their name be wiped out in the next generation.|Preserves extinction and the specified generational horizon.
109:14|Let the guilt of his fathers be remembered before the LORD;\nlet his mother’s sin never be erased.|Keeps both parental lines and opposed remembrance/erasure.
109:15|Let these sins always remain before the LORD,\nand let him cut off their memory from the earth,|Clarifies sins as the remembered object while preserving extinction of memory.
109:16|because he never thought to show faithful love.\nHe pursued a poor and needy man,\na brokenhearted man, to put him to death.|Keeps the stated reason, victim's vulnerability, and lethal intent.
109:17|He loved cursing, and it came upon him;\nhe took no pleasure in blessing, and it stayed far from him.|Retains the source's narrative reversal rather than making every clause a wish.
109:18|He wore cursing like a garment;\nit entered him like water,\nlike oil into his bones.|Preserves clothing and inward penetration images.
109:19|Let it be the robe he wraps around himself,\nthe belt he wears continually.|Keeps the shift to a wish and both clothing objects.
109:20|Let this be the LORD’s payment to my accusers,\nto those who speak evil against my life.|Retains reward/payment language and plural accusers' return.
109:21|But you, LORD, my Lord, act for me for your name’s sake.\nBecause your faithful love is good, rescue me.|Preserves both divine names and the grounds of appeal.
109:22|For I am poor and needy,\nand my heart is wounded within me.|Keeps social vulnerability and internal wound.
109:23|I fade like a lengthening shadow;\nI am shaken off like a locust.|Preserves two distinct frailty comparisons.
109:24|My knees give way from fasting;\nmy body has wasted away, with no fat left.|Keeps bodily effects of fasting without spiritualizing them.
109:25|I have become an object of scorn to them;\nwhen they see me, they shake their heads.|Retains visible contempt and the head gesture.
109:26|Help me, LORD my God;\nsave me in keeping with your faithful love.|Keeps the paired pleas and covenant-love measure.
109:27|Let them know that this is your hand,\nthat you, LORD, have done it.|Preserves hand metaphor and emphatic divine agency.
109:28|They may curse, but you will bless.\nWhen they rise against me, let them be ashamed;\nlet your servant rejoice.|Keeps curse/blessing contrast and opponents/servant outcomes.
109:29|Let my accusers be clothed in disgrace;\nlet them wrap themselves in shame as in a cloak.|Returns to the clothing image with both shame terms.
109:30|With my mouth I will greatly thank the LORD;\nin the midst of the crowd I will praise him.|Preserves bodily and public thanksgiving.
109:31|For he stands at the right hand of the needy\nto save him from those who condemn him to death.|Keeps the right-hand reversal of verse 6 and judicial threat to life.

110:1|Of David. A psalm.
The LORD’s declaration to my lord:
“Sit at my right hand
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”|Preserves title, distinct LORD/lord, and subjugation image without naming the addressee.
110:2|The LORD will extend your mighty staff from Zion:\n“Rule in the midst of your enemies.”|Keeps the royal staff, Zion, and imperative to rule amid foes.

110:3|Your people offer themselves freely on the day you muster your strength.\nIn holy splendor, from the womb of dawn,\nthe dew of your youth is yours.|Preserves the difficult youth/dew/dawn imagery without resolving all syntax.
110:4|The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind:\n“You are a priest forever,\nin the manner of Melchizedek.”|Retains enduring priesthood and the difficult Melchizedek formula with a note.
110:5|The Lord is at your right hand;\nhe crushes kings on the day of his anger.|Preserves Adonai rather than inserting YHWH and retains crushed kings.
110:6|He judges among the nations, leaving them full of corpses;\nhe crushes heads across a vast land.|Keeps lethal judgment and the broad land image without sanitizing corpses.
110:7|He drinks from a stream beside the road;\ntherefore he lifts his head.|Retains unnamed subject and the unexplained therefore connection.
111:1|Praise YAH!\nI will thank the LORD with my whole heart,\nin the company of the upright and in the assembly.|Keeps opening acclamation and two communal settings.
111:2|Great are the LORD’s works,\nstudied by all who delight in them.|Preserves attentive pursuit of works rather than passive admiration.
111:3|His work is splendor and majesty;\nhis righteousness stands forever.|Retains paired glory terms and enduring righteousness.
111:4|He has made his wonders remembered;\nthe LORD is gracious and compassionate.|Keeps divine provision of remembrance and paired attributes.
111:5|He gives food to those who fear him;\nhe remembers his covenant forever.|Retains food and covenant remembrance without an added condition.
111:6|He has shown his people the power of his works\nby giving them the inheritance of nations.|Preserves territorial gift as the displayed power.
111:7|The works of his hands are faithfulness and justice;\nall his precepts are trustworthy,|Keeps hands, paired qualities, and precepts terminology.
111:8|firmly established forever and ever,\nenacted in faithfulness and uprightness.|Carries preceding precepts into the enduring and ethical description.
111:9|He sent redemption to his people;\nhe ordained his covenant forever.\nHoly and fearsome is his name.|Preserves three poetic units and reverent fear, not merely admiration.

111:10|Fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.\nAll who practice his precepts have good understanding.\nHis praise stands forever.|Makes the implied practiced commands legible while preserving three final units.
112:1|Praise YAH!\nHappy is the one who fears the LORD,\nwho delights greatly in his commands.|Preserves singular exemplar and strong delight alongside fear.
112:2|His offspring will be mighty in the land;\nthe generation of the upright will be blessed.|Keeps offspring and generation claims distinct.
112:3|Wealth and riches are in his house,\nand his righteousness stands forever.|Retains material wealth without turning the psalm into a formula.
112:4|Light dawns in the darkness for the upright,\nfor one who is gracious, compassionate, and righteous.|Takes the virtues of the upright person while recording the possible divine reference.
112:5|It goes well for one who is generous and lends,\nwho manages his affairs with justice.|Keeps lending, generosity, and just conduct together.
112:6|He will never be shaken;\nthe righteous will be remembered forever.|Preserves stability and lasting memory.
112:7|He does not fear bad news;\nhis heart is steadfast, trusting the LORD.|Keeps feared report, steady heart, and trust.
112:8|His heart is secure; he will not fear,\nuntil he looks in triumph on his foes.|Retains until and the conventional victorious look without adding destruction.
112:9|He gives freely to the needy;\nhis righteousness stands forever;\nhis horn is raised in honor.|Preserves three units and the ancient horn image with vocabulary support.
112:10|The wicked see it and rage;\nthey grind their teeth and waste away.\nThe desire of the wicked comes to nothing.|Keeps the bodily anger and vanishing desire in three units.
113:1|Praise YAH!\nPraise, you servants of the LORD;\npraise the name of the LORD.|Retains all three praise calls and divine-name forms.
113:2|Let the name of the LORD be blessed\nfrom now and forever.|Keeps the present-to-endless temporal span.
113:3|From the rising of the sun to its setting,\nthe name of the LORD is to be praised.|Preserves the geographic and daily resonance of sunrise/sunset.
113:4|The LORD is high above all nations;\nhis glory is above the heavens.|Keeps two elevated scopes.
113:5|Who is like the LORD our God,\nenthroned on high,|Retains the open question across the following verse.
113:6|who stoops to look\non the heavens and the earth?|Keeps the surprising lowering needed even to see heaven.
113:7|He raises the poor from the dust\nand lifts the needy from the refuse heap,|Preserves material degradation and upward movement.
113:8|to seat them with nobles,\nwith the nobles of his people.|Retains repeated nobles and the social reversal.
113:9|He settles the childless woman in a home\nas a joyful mother of children.\nPraise YAH!|Keeps the woman's changed circumstance and concluding acclamation.
114:1|When Israel came out of Egypt,\nthe house of Jacob from a people of strange speech,|Preserves ancestral parallelism and linguistic estrangement.
114:2|Judah became his sanctuary,\nIsrael his domain.|Keeps sanctuary and rule as distinct metaphors.
114:3|The sea saw it and fled;\nthe Jordan turned back.|Preserves personified water reactions without specifying what was seen.
114:4|The mountains skipped like rams,\nthe hills like lambs.|Keeps differentiated terrain and animals.
114:5|What happened to you, sea, that you fled?\nAnd to you, Jordan, that you turned back?|Retains direct address and repeated questions.
114:6|Mountains, why did you skip like rams,\nand you hills, like lambs?|Carries the question into the repeated animal comparison.

141:9|Keep me from the grip of the trap they have laid for me,\nfrom the snares of evildoers.|Keeps trap's hand/grip and plural snares.
141:10|Let the wicked fall together into their nets\nwhile I pass through.|Retains collective fall and speaker's passage, with pronoun uncertainty noted.

142:1|A maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.\nWith my voice I cry to the LORD;\nwith my voice I plead with the LORD.|Binds separate title and first body record, retaining cave and repeated voice/name.
142:2|I pour out my complaint before him;\nI tell my trouble before him.|Preserves doubled before-him and pouring image.
142:3|When my spirit grows faint within me,\nyou yourself know my path.\nOn the road I walk, they have hidden a trap for me.|Keeps divine knowledge amid weakness and hidden danger.
142:4|Look to my right and see:\nno one acknowledges me.\nNo refuge remains for me; no one cares for my life.|Preserves imperative, right side, and repeated abandonment.
142:5|I cry to you, LORD;\nI say, “You are my refuge,\nmy portion in the land of the living.”|Keeps refuge and inheritance metaphors within living land.
142:6|Attend to my cry, for I am brought very low.\nRescue me from my pursuers,\nfor they are stronger than I am.|Preserves both reasons for urgent rescue.
142:7|Bring my life out of confinement so I may thank your name.\nThe righteous will gather around me,\nfor you will deal generously with me.|Keeps confinement image without assuming a literal jail.
143:1|A psalm of David.\nLORD, hear my prayer; listen to my pleas.\nIn your faithfulness answer me, in your righteousness.|Preserves title and paired appeals grounded in divine attributes.
143:2|Do not enter into judgment with your servant,\nfor no living person is righteous before you.|Keeps judicial plea and universal living-person claim.
143:3|The enemy pursues my life;\nhe crushes me to the ground\nand makes me dwell in darkness like those long dead.|Preserves violent pursuit and prolonged-death comparison.
143:4|My spirit grows faint within me;\nmy heart is appalled inside me.|Keeps two inward organs and distinct distress terms.
143:5|I remember the days of old;\nI meditate on all you have done\nand ponder the work of your hands.|Preserves remembrance and two reflection verbs.
143:6|I spread my hands toward you;\nmy whole being thirsts for you like parched land. Selah.|Keeps bodily gesture, dry-earth comparison, and marker.
143:7|Answer me quickly, LORD; my spirit is failing.\nDo not hide your face from me,\nor I will become like those who go down to the Pit.|Preserves urgency, hidden face, and underworld comparison.
143:8|Let me hear your faithful love in the morning, for I trust in you.\nMake known the way I should walk,\nfor to you I lift my whole being.|Keeps morning hearing, path guidance, and lifted life.
143:9|Rescue me from my enemies, LORD;\nto you I flee for shelter.|Renders difficult covered-to-you expression as seeking shelter with note.
143:10|Teach me to do your will, for you are my God.\nLet your good spirit lead me on level ground.|Keeps obedience request and spatial guidance image.
143:11|For your name’s sake, LORD, keep me alive;\nin your righteousness bring my life out of trouble.|Preserves name and righteousness as parallel grounds.
143:12|In your faithful love, put an end to my enemies;\ndestroy all who afflict my life,\nfor I am your servant.|Keeps lethal petition and servant rationale without softening.
144:1|Of David.\nBlessed be the LORD, my rock,\nwho trains my hands for battle, my fingers for war.|Preserves title and actual martial training.

144:2|He is my faithful love and my fortress,
my stronghold and my deliverer,
my shield, in whom I take refuge,
who subdues my people under me.|Keeps stacked metaphors and singular my people of the pinned text.
144:3|LORD, what is a human being that you know him,\na mortal that you take account of him?|Preserves parallel human frailty and divine attention.
144:4|A human being is like a breath;\nhis days are like a passing shadow.|Keeps two transience images.
144:5|LORD, bend your heavens and come down;\ntouch the mountains so they smoke.|Preserves cosmic descent and smoking touch.
144:6|Flash lightning and scatter them;\nsend your arrows and throw them into confusion.|Keeps divine weapons and two hostile outcomes.
144:7|Stretch your hands down from on high;\nfree me and rescue me from mighty waters,\nfrom the hand of foreigners,|Preserves divine hands, drowning image, and human hand.
144:8|whose mouths speak falsehood\nand whose right hand is a hand of lies.|Keeps mouth and oath-hand imagery without adding an explicit oath.
144:9|God, I will sing you a new song;\non a ten-stringed harp I will make music for you,|Preserves new song and exact instrument-string count.
144:10|you who give kings victory,\nwho free David your servant from the deadly sword.|Keeps royal rescue and David's explicit third-person name.
144:11|Free me and rescue me from the hand of foreigners,\nwhose mouths speak falsehood\nand whose right hand is a hand of lies.|Preserves the repeated appeal and description of verses 7–8.
144:12|May our sons be like plants grown tall in their youth,\nour daughters like corner pillars carved for a palace.|Keeps both gendered images and takes the transition as communal wish.

144:13|May our storehouses be full, supplying every kind of produce;\nmay our flocks multiply by thousands and tens of thousands in our fields.|Preserves abundance, both numerical scales, and outdoor flocks.
144:14|May our cattle be laden with increase;\nmay there be no breach, no going out,\nno cry of distress in our squares.|Keeps difficult laden-cattle and civic phrases open with alternatives noted.
